status: User accepted the 1 exact diagnostic sites on 2026-10-07. Focused qualification and its recorded limits are unchanged. Full RPM and native architecture qualification remain separate gates.
root_cause: The inlined BindAccumulator warning originates at VisitTestTypeOf result. Every declared literal flag initializes the result or terminates at kOther. GCC additionally considers unnamed enum values.
source_review: The actual TYPEOF_LITERAL_LIST has eight recognized type names and kOther. BytecodeGenerator emits CompareTypeOf only for recognized flags; kOther emits LoadFalse instead. VisitTestTypeOf handles each recognized flag and rejects kOther. No accepted bytecode path reaches BindAccumulator with an uninitialized result.

coverage.native_modes: 810000 cases per release/debug run, normally and under Valgrind. All eight recognized flags across ten modeled ordinary input categories, plus kOther rejection without allocations.
coverage.memory: Both Valgrind runs have zero errors; all 1190002 allocations are freed in each.
coverage.compiler: Each GCC13 control build reproduces the same result maybe-uninitialized diagnostic.
coverage.actual_javascript: All nine type strings over 20 real JavaScript values, including NaN, Infinity, null, boxed primitives and callable/noncallable proxies. TurboFan optimization is explicitly requested and verified with runtime.h kOptimized/kTurboFanned bits. --no-turbolev retains the BytecodeGraphBuilder frontend.

limits: The enum/macro and dispatch body are verbatim extracts. The standalone graph evaluator models predicate results with owned nodes; it does not emit machine code.
Ordinary Node value categories are covered; browser-only exotic undetectable objects are outside this control.
UNREACHABLE becomes a typed test exception so rejection and allocation cleanup can be observed. Production behavior is unchanged.
The first JavaScript run requested optimization without checking its final state; the retained second run adds those assertions and is the qualified result.
Compiler flags and visible warnings remain unchanged; no suppression or runtime patch is proposed.
